plan.topic: Thanksgiving leftovers when tirzepatide means smaller portions: how long leftovers keep in the fridge and freezer, per US food-safety guidance
plan.angle:
20:00 holiday-table Short. Follow the task's length arm and hook archetype.
- Sentence 1 (14 words or fewer): 'On tirzepatide, Thanksgiving leftovers may outlast your appetite. Here's how long they keep.' Scene 1's on-screen text matches it.
- By 6 s: refrigerate within 2 hours, and eat refrigerated leftovers within 3 to 4 days (FoodSafety.gov/USDA, copied exactly with the page's live date).
- Second fact: freeze portions for longer storage, worded only as the USDA page prints it.
- Separate label sentence, no 'so': tirzepatide reduces appetite and food intake.
- Untagged tips, 2 at most: box small portions straight away; label containers with the date.
- No guilt, no 'bad' foods, no calorie talk.
- Safety line: vomiting or diarrhoea you can't keep up with means contact your prescriber (the label links fluid loss to kidney problems). Then the scoped don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and a loop line.
- Note that rules elsewhere may differ, but use no extra country sources.
- Post note: the related-video target is the Thanksgiving long video.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide and Thanksgiving Leftovers: How Long Do They Keep? #shorts
plan.why: The holiday-table slot runs through 11-27, and search peaks the week of Nov 23. Leftovers is the only holiday moment from the playbook list not yet made, and it's a practical moment that feeds the Thanksgiving long video.

package.title: Tirzepatide: Thanksgiving Leftovers Keep All Week? #shorts
package.description:
A smaller appetite on tirzepatide doesn't change the USDA leftover clock: fridge 3–4 days, freezer 3–4 months for best quality. That's US guidance; rules elsewhere may differ.
#Tirzepatide #Thanksgiving #FoodSafety
Severe stomach pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting, means call your prescriber right away. For anything that isn't an emergency sign, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

script.cta: No subscribe line and no 'link in the description', per the Shorts ending rule from 11-17. The Short ends with the scoped don't-stop line, then 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.', then the loop line 'Next time the fridge fills up:', which runs back into sentence 1. WORD COUNT: 159 spoken words (my own count), inside the standard arm's 135–160. POST NOTE (Exp G): the related-video target is the Thanksgiving long video (food or holiday → Thanksgiving). PRE-PUBLISH CHECK (still needed): the FSIS page returns 403 to automated fetches. The 2-hour, 3–4 day and 3–4 month figures, and the 'best quality' reading, are backed by an FSIS-sourced search snippet and the archived FSIS fact sheet. The 'Last Updated 31 Jul 2020' date has not been checked by machine. Someone needs to open the page in a browser and confirm that date. If the page shows a different date, use that one.

factcheck.summary: I checked every number and label claim, and they hold up. I loaded the Zepbound label (Revised 8/2026). Section 12.2 says word for word: "Tirzepatide decreases calorie intake. The effects are likely mediated by affecting appetite." Section 5.3 is Acute Kidney Injury Due to Volume Depletion, linked to stomach side effects (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) that lead to dehydration. Section 5.5 is Acute Pancreatitis, with "persistent or severe abdominal pain". I also loaded the Mounjaro label (Revised 8/2026). Its Section 5.2 is Acute Pancreatitis ("…may or may not be accompanied by nausea or vomiting") and its Section 5.5 is Acute Kidney Injury Due to Volume Depletion, so the section numbers in the source titles are right and every listed section is used. The USDA FSIS page returns 403 (blocked) to my fetch tool, as the script's own note warns, so I couldn't open it directly. Search-index text from that exact URL confirms the 2-hour rule (1 hour above 90 °F), splitting food into shallow containers, 3–4 days in the fridge and 3–4 months frozen. It also confirms the frozen-leftovers note that supports "best quality" ("safe indefinitely… lose moisture and flavor"), and shows "Last Updated: Jul 31, 2020", which matches the source entry. I counted the spoken words myself: 159, inside the 135–160 standard arm. The safety beats are in place: the severe-stomach-pain line keeps "with or without vomiting" and "right away", and the scoped don't-stop line and "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber." are both spoken and shown on screen. There is no subscribe line and no "link in the description" line. There are no fluid tips, so the limit-fluids caveat isn't needed. The script includes a US-only caveat, which matters because the UK Food Standards Agency (FSA) advises eating leftovers within 2 days. The title's promise is delivered. There are 4 minor wording fixes below. Before publishing, someone should still open the FSIS page in a browser.
